{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOV5s7_c8AAAABi65UnA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bs-hLzhMRIUk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bs-hL", "number": 11, "title": "Polish player UI: speaker mute icon, stable status feedback, and fullscreen save management", "body": "## Goal and scope

Polish the existing nes-rust-neo browser player with three related UI/UX changes: replace the text mute button with the SNES-style speaker icon, prevent transient status messages from shifting the player or touch controls, and make the existing save-state and save-data management accessible during fullscreen play. Build on the UI delivered by #3, #7 and #9. Preserve the simple snes-rust-derived design and existing NES/FDS behavior; this is a focused frontend improvement, not a new emulator feature or save-storage redesign.

### 1. Speaker icon instead of Mute/Unmute text

- Follow the existing [snes-rust HTML](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html), [CSS](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/style.css) and [audio UI logic](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js). Use an inline SVG speaker with sound waves when audible and a crossed/muted speaker when muted, centered in a compact 44×44 CSS-pixel button. No external icon dependency.
- In the NES frontend, `web/src/index.html` currently has a text-only `#mute`, `web/src/main.js` updates its text content, and `web/src/style.css` assigns a wider width to it together with Play. Adapt these without affecting the Play button.
- Preserve the existing mute toggle, remembered last audible volume, slider synchronization (including zero), persisted preferences, audio activation/retry and keyboard/touch behavior. Update the accessible name (Mute/Unmute), pressed state and tooltip as appropriate. Do not rely on color alone.

### 2. Stable gameplay layout during transient feedback

- Currently `notice()` in [main.js](https://github.com/takahirox/nes-rust-neo/blob/main/web/src/main.js) updates `#status` and may clear it after a timeout. [style.css](https://github.com/takahirox/nes-rust-neo/blob/main/web/src/style.css) hides empty status and makes it a full-width toolbar row on mobile. This can change the layout height when save/load feedback appears or disappears, shifting the touch D-pad, A/B, Start and Select buttons during play.
- Reproduce and eliminate this layout shift. Use compact non-layout-affecting feedback (e.g. a positioned, non-intercepting toast in the player or a genuinely fixed-size reserved status area). Keep the video, controls and touch targets stationary when ordinary transient notices appear, change length, wrap, replace one another or clear. Keep text readable on narrow screens; do not obscure game controls, disk controls or important content, intercept gameplay touches, steal focus, or cause scrolling.
- Apply the same stable feedback behavior in normal and fullscreen presentation, including save/load success, recovery-profile notices and ordinary errors. Retain accessible status announcements and meaningful persistent warnings/retry actions for actual save failures; do not hide errors or remove existing data-protection behavior just to prevent layout shifts. A user deliberately opening a management dialog or changing orientation is not a transient-notice layout shift.

### 3. Save management during fullscreen

- Currently `#state-controls` and `#save-data` are outside `#game-presentation`, and fullscreen marks player chrome inert. Make the existing save controls usable without exiting fullscreen, on desktop and touch devices in portrait and landscape. Provide the same shared **Save state selector | Save | Load** workflow, including New state, screenshot/timestamp history, selection, overwrite, deletion, import/export and appropriate feedback.
- Also expose **Save data** profile management where applicable (battery-backed NES and FDS): select, create, duplicate, remove, import/export and access recovery profiles. Non-battery games do not need the profile selector. Preserve existing save semantics and protections; do not create separate fullscreen saves or a different state selection.
- Reuse existing components, dialogs, handlers and storage logic where practical (e.g. shared controls arranged within the fullscreen subtree, or a shared compact disclosure). Ensure dialogs and confirmation/file-picker workflows are usable from fullscreen, including correct focus/keyboard access and dismissal. Avoid explicitly exiting fullscreen to perform these actions; account for browser-imposed native picker behavior without claiming control over it. Maintain selection and playback intent when entering/exiting fullscreen and when opening/dismissing the picker.
- Keep the video area prominent. Avoid unnecessary persistent chrome, especially in short landscape. Reserve stable space or use unobtrusive overlays that do not cover touch gameplay targets; all NES touch buttons, fullscreen exit and existing conditional FDS side/eject controls must remain usable. No separate settings page, unrelated toolbar redesign, new save format or core changes.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Audio UI:** Build and run the existing Chromium browser suite with focused tests for the icon button. Verify the two visible SVG states, accessible name/pressed state, keyboard and touch activation, slider zero/nonzero synchronization, mute/unmute restoring the previous audible volume, persisted preference after reload and unchanged audio behavior. Compare with the SNES reference; button is compact, with a 44×44 touch target and no visible Mute/Unmute text.
- [ ] **Layout stability regression:** Reproduce the reported issue on the baseline where practical and add an automated real-browser regression with a loaded game and touch-enabled mobile viewport. Record `getBoundingClientRect()` for the canvas/picture, D-pad, individual directional buttons, A/B, Start/Select and relevant controls before saving, while success feedback is visible, after it expires, and during a second save/load with different-length feedback. Repeat on narrow portrait and short landscape, in normal and fullscreen views, with representative NES and FDS media. Expected: identical positions and sizes within subpixel rounding (at most 1 CSS px), unchanged scroll offset, no blocked touch targets and no stuck input. Exercise a long recovery notice and an ordinary failure message as well; keep existing actionable save warnings available. Record actual measurements or test assertions and screenshots. No requirement to redesign unrelated persistent warning UI.
- [ ] **Fullscreen saves:** Using the actual Wasm build and existing lawful fixtures, enter fullscreen, select/create a state, Save, overwrite, choose another, Load, remove and import/export via the shared picker. Verify real restored gameplay, state selection and manual pause intent, correct feedback, safe cancellation, and no app-triggered fullscreen exit. Check battery and FDS profile selection, creation/duplication, management and recovery access; confirm profile/state identity remains shared with the normal view and FDS side status restores correctly. Check disabled/unavailable operations and an ordinary storage failure. Native file picker limitations may be documented and tested without requiring unsupported browser capabilities.
- [ ] **Responsive/accessibility checks:** Inspect desktop, narrow touch portrait and short touch landscape screenshots in normal and fullscreen modes. Expected: no unintended layout shift, clipped or overlapping controls; game picture, touch pad, fullscreen exit and FDS controls remain accessible. Verify dialog focus, keyboard navigation and return to the appropriate control on dismissal; notifications do not intercept pointer input. Preserve existing CRT/Pixel, display, audio, play/pause/reset and save protection.
- [ ] **Validation:** Run the current README build/test commands and mandatory CI, including `npm --prefix web ci`, `npm --prefix web run build`, `npm --prefix web test` (with documented Chromium installation), `node tests/check-static.mjs` and `git diff --check`. All required checks pass on the final revision, including existing NES/FDS save-state, profile, touch, audio and fullscreen regressions. Record focused tests and screenshots in the PR or linked validation document. Update README/Help briefly if needed. No mandatory human confirmation is required. Keep scope proportionate: fix demonstrated supported-use issues, not speculative compound failures or unrelated refactors.

## Post-merge verification

- After merging to `main` and closing this Issue, verify the GitHub Pages deployment succeeds and record the Actions run and published URL (expected https://takahirox.github.io/nes-rust-neo/).
- Smoke-test the live player with local lawful test media: speaker icon and mute/volume behavior, state save/load feedback without moving the touch controls, and save-state/profile access in fullscreen (NES and FDS as applicable). Expected: correct existing save behavior, stable controls, accessible dialogs, no unexpected console errors or unintended fullscreen exit.
- Record results in the merged PR or closed Issue. Open a linked follow-up Issue for any publication-only defect; do not block merge on future live-site checks.
